A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain the main text and Appendices A–E. Their figures, tables, equations and appendix material can be reliably matched despite pagination and spacing changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original distillation experiments, including accuracy comparisons, out-of-domain evaluation, teacher-count analyses and GPU-hour measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main comparisons and the six-teacher MMLU evaluation in Appendix D.3 and Table 15.

M1.justification: The five purification methods, training objectives, routing procedures and RL teacher-selection algorithm are unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–B.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate OBQA, ARC, RiddleSense and PubMedQA, out-of-domain PIQA and BioASQ, and MMLU. The broader task coverage and six-teacher experiment in Appendix D.3 already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. The main comparisons retain inference, fine-tuning, Distilling-Step-by-Step and TinyLLM; Appendix C.3 retains the ABKD evaluation. TwT remains discussed but unevaluated.

E3.justification: Dataset partitions, student and teacher configurations, training settings, accuracy and CMV metrics, and efficiency-measurement procedures are unchanged. Table 7 and the experimental settings in Section 5 and Appendices B–D are retained.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same aggregator comparison in Table 6, incremental teacher-count analyses in Tables 9–14, out-of-domain tests and OBQA case study in Figure 5. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting without repeated-run counts, seed details, error bars, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results, rankings and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains the 783M teacher-selection average of 67.55%, and Table 15 retains the similarity router's MMLU accuracy of 55.26%.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, CMV definition, and Proposition 1 with its proof in Appendix B.2 are unchanged. Replacing 'Conflict Mitigation Value' with 'CMV' in Section 5.3 only abbreviates an existing term.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: knowledge purification, five implementations, conflict mitigation, improved distillation and routing-based generalization. Their scientific scope and strength are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of aggregation performance, routing generalization and student-size effects are retained. Section 6 and Appendix D.3 preserve the same limitations concerning teacher-ensemble size, computational resources and broader applicability.

D1.justification: Experimental prompts, implementation details, hyperparameters, Algorithm 1 and the four-A100 hardware disclosure are unchanged. Appendix E's revised LLM-use statement concerns manuscript editing, not experimental implementation or reproducibility.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to distillation and routing research are unchanged. Bibliographic differences consist of line wrapping and pagination, without added or removed references.

P1.justification: Appendix E is retitled and rewritten: v1 denies LLM use for writing or polishing, whereas v2 reports post-drafting linguistic assistance. v2 also adds funding acknowledgments, marks Pengpeng Shao as a corresponding author, updates email presentation and abbreviates CMV in Section 5.3.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is slightly reduced and spacing separates its caption from Table 3's caption, which overlaps it in v1. Other main-text tables receive small spacing adjustments, and references and appendices are repaginated. Figure and table content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes the overlapping Figure 3 and Table 3 captions on page 8, improving readability. It also adds funding information and explicitly describes LLM assistance with language editing. These are limited presentation and transparency gains; the scientific evidence, methods and conclusions remain unchanged.
